opt_compat_section.description: Settings section heading for the compatibility mode switch.

opt_compat_mode_label.message: Where this device publishes its data

opt_compat_mode_desc.message: Every device in one sync group must pick the same mode. Switching does not move existing files: the new folder starts empty and this device re-uploads its own data.

opt_compat_mode_isolated.message: Own file names — konode folder + kesonode_* files

opt_compat_mode_standalone.message: Fully separate — Kesonode folder + kesonode_* files

locale_bcp47.description: NOT a sentence: the BCP 47 tag for THIS catalogue, written into <html lang> so the browser and screen readers know what language the page is in. Replace it with your own tag and nothing else, lowercase language and uppercase region: de, es, pt-BR, zh-CN. Do not translate the word.

extension_name.message: Kesonode | Private Bookmark & Tab Sync v1.5.22
extension_name.description: The extension's name. This IS the Chrome Web Store listing title, so it carries the search terms people actually type: bookmark, tab, sync. Keep 'Kesonode' first and keep the whole thing under 45 characters. Translate the part after the bar into what someone would search for in your language; leave 'Kesonode' alone, it is the product name.

extension_description.message: Privacy-first browser sync to your own storage: Google Drive, WebDAV, GitHub.
extension_description.description: Shown in the browser's extension list, and used as the store summary when the listing does not override it.

datatype_bookmarks.description: One of the four data types. Also a section heading in Settings.

datatype_history.description: One of the four data types.

datatype_sessions.description: One of the four data types: the tabs a device has open.

datatype_extensions.description: One of the four data types: the list of installed extensions.

status_idle.description: Sync status: nothing is happening and nothing is wrong. Not 'finished'. This is the resting state.

status_syncing.description: Sync status: a sync is running now.

status_success.description: Sync status: the last sync completed.

status_error.description: Sync status: the last sync failed.

status_conflict.description: Sync status: a conflict is waiting for the user to choose a version.

stream_off.description: Per-data-type state, shown in a tooltip after the type name: this type is turned off in Settings. Lower case: it follows 'Bookmarks: '.

stream_syncing.description: Per-data-type state: this type is being synced right now.

stream_pending.description: Per-data-type state: a sync is running but has not reached this type yet.

stream_never.description: Per-data-type state: this type has never completed a sync. Must not sound like success.

stream_stale.description: Per-data-type state: this type has synced before, but the most recent attempt failed.

stream_synced.description: Per-data-type state: this type synced successfully.

popup_settings_aria.description: Accessible name of the gear button in the popup's top-right corner.

popup_sync_now.description: The popup's primary button. While a sync runs it shows status_syncing instead.

popup_load_error.message: Couldn't reach Kesonode. Tap to retry.
popup_load_error.description: The popup could not read its own state. The whole banner is a button, hence 'tap to retry'.

popup_recovery_notice.message: An unusual deletion ($COUNT$ bookmarks) was blocked and a restore point was saved. Apply it or keep them in Settings → Activity.
popup_recovery_notice.description: The mass-delete guard refused a peer's deletions. Reassuring by design: nothing was lost. Said 'Review in' until there was something to decide there; now the banner leads to a real choice, so it names it. 'Settings → Activity' names a tab, so it must match the tab's own translation.

popup_guard_notice.message: Publishing is paused: this device's bookmarks keep changing ($COUNT$ entries this cycle). Nothing was lost; a restore point was saved and publishing resumes on its own once the tree settles. See Settings → Activity.
popup_guard_notice.description: The local change guard held this device's own bookmark upload because the local tree changed by more than the cap on several consecutive sync cycles. Reassuring by design: nothing was deleted, and no action is needed because it resumes automatically. 'Settings → Activity' names a tab, so it must match the tab's own translation.

popup_no_backend.description: No storage provider has been set up yet. The banner opens Settings.

popup_setup_title.description: First-run card in the popup, shown until a storage provider is chosen. The button opens the setup wizard.

popup_setup_body.message: Choose where your data is stored. Nothing is synced or uploaded until you do.
popup_setup_body.description: Body of the first-run card. The second sentence is a promise about data and must be translated literally.

popup_setup_cta.description: Button on the first-run card. Opens the setup wizard in a new tab.

popup_keep_local.description: Conflict resolution: keep what this device has.

popup_keep_local_title.message: Keep this device: $DEVICE$'s changes are not applied here
popup_keep_local_title.description: Tooltip on the keep button. $DEVICE$ is the other device's name.

popup_use_remote.description: Conflict resolution: take the other device's version.

popup_use_remote_title.message: Use the other device: merge $DEVICE$'s changes into this one
popup_use_remote_title.description: Tooltip on the use-the-other button. $DEVICE$ is the other device's name.

popup_conflict_resolve.description: Button on a conflict card in the popup, next to the other device's name. Opens Settings → Activity, which lists what differs between the two devices and offers the same two answers.

popup_active_streams.description: Heading above the four data-type dots. The stylesheet displays it in capitals, so do not capitalise it here.

popup_guard_detail.message: $COUNT$ changed this cycle · cap $CAP$ · $ROUNDS$ cycles in a row
popup_guard_detail.description: Shown under the guard banner with the live numbers: entries changed this cycle, the cap, and how many consecutive cycles the tree has been changing. Auto-filled, not translated.

popup_guard_coexist.message: This usually means Kesonode is running alongside your browser's own bookmark sync. Use one sync system for bookmarks, or Exclude bookmarks from sync (Settings → Data types) to keep a folder another tool owns out of Kesonode.
popup_guard_coexist.description: First-time tip under the guard banner. Reassuring by design: normally two sync systems touch the same tree. 'Settings → Data types' names a tab, so it must match the tab's own translation.

popup_guard_dismiss.description: Button that dismisses the one-time coexist tip under the guard banner.

opt_guard_section.description: Heading of the Settings → Advanced section for the local change guard.

opt_guard_label.message: Pause publishing on runaway bookmark changes
opt_guard_label.description: Toggle label for the local change guard.

opt_guard_desc.message: When this device's bookmarks change by a large amount on several cycles in a row, hold back its upload until the tree settles. Prevents a runaway sync or extension from broadcasting a half-finished rewrite to every peer. A single bulk edit still publishes immediately.
opt_guard_desc.description: Toggle description for the local change guard.

opt_guard_cap_label.description: Label for the guard threshold slider.

opt_guard_cap_desc.message: A cycle is a large change above this many bookmark entries, or 30% of the tree — whichever is larger. Raise it if you routinely import or reorganize big folders.
opt_guard_cap_desc.description: Description for the guard threshold slider.

popup_missing_extensions_one.description: Exactly one extension is installed on another device but not on this one.

popup_missing_extensions_other.description: More than one extension is installed on another device but not on this one. In languages that use the singular after a numeral, this is the same wording as the _one form.

popup_open_all.description: Opens a store page for every missing extension, one tab each.

popup_sessions_head.description: Heading above the restorable sessions list. The stylesheet displays it in capitals, so do not capitalise it here.

popup_unknown_device.description: Fallback name for a peer device whose session carries no label.

popup_tabs_one.description: How many tabs a peer's session holds, in the case of exactly one.

popup_tabs_other.description: How many tabs a peer's session holds. In languages that use the singular after a numeral, this is the same wording as the _one form.

popup_restore.description: Opens the tabs of a peer device's session. Adds tabs; removes nothing.

popup_rate_body.message: Kesonode has been syncing your devices for a while now. If it works for you, a rating in the store helps other people find it.

popup_restore_confirm_one.description: The Restore button after a first press, on a session large enough to ask first: the second press opens this many tabs. Exactly one; never shown in practice, since only large sessions ask.

popup_restore_confirm_other.description: The Restore button after a first press, on a session large enough to ask first: the second press opens this many tabs. Keep it short, it is a button. In languages that use the singular after a numeral, this is the same wording as the _one form.

popup_tabs_open_here_one.description: Beside a peer's session in the popup: how many of its tabs are already open in this browser, so Restore will not open them again. In the case of exactly one.

popup_tabs_open_here_other.description: Beside a peer's session in the popup: how many of its tabs are already open in this browser, so Restore will not open them again. In languages that use the singular after a numeral, this is the same wording as the _one form.

popup_restore_all_open.description: The Restore button, disabled, when every tab of the session is already open in this browser. Keep it short, it is a button.

popup_backend_label.description: Footer label before the storage provider's name.

popup_backend_none.description: Footer value when no storage provider is set up.

popup_device_label.description: Footer label before this device's name.

popup_configure.description: Footer link to Settings. Keep the arrow.

popup_activity_log.description: Footer link that opens Settings on the Activity tab. Keep the arrow.

common_show.description: Tooltip on the eye button that reveals a password.

common_hide.description: Tooltip on the eye button that hides a password again.

provider_gdrive_desc.message: Syncs straight to your own Google Drive. Thanks to OAuth, the access token is kept on this device only.

provider_nextcloud_desc.message: Your own Nextcloud or ownCloud server.

provider_nextcloud_note.message: Enter just your server host; use an App Password (Settings → Security).
provider_nextcloud_note.description: Extra hint shown under the card once it is selected.

provider_pcloud_desc.message: pCloud storage. Needs a paid pCloud plan.

provider_pcloud_note.message: Pick the $REGION$ region if that is where your pCloud account lives.

provider_koofr_note.message: Use your Koofr email as the username, and a Koofr app password as the password.

provider_fastmail_note.message: Use your full Fastmail address as the username, and an app password that has Files (WebDAV) access.

provider_jianguoyun_desc.message: Nutstore cloud storage, widely used in mainland China.

provider_jianguoyun_note.message: Use your Nutstore email as the username, and a third-party app password as the password. On a free account, raise Sync interval to 120 seconds or more once you have three devices: Nutstore allows 600 WebDAV requests every 30 minutes.

provider_github_desc.message: Your synced data lives in a private GitHub repository, which Kesonode reaches with a Personal Access Token.

provider_webdav_desc.message: Synology, kDrive, or any other WebDAV server.

provider_syncing_to.description: $URL$ is rendered in a monospace <code> element, so the sentence is split at the placeholder rather than interpolated. Keep the placeholder as one piece.

onb_welcome_subtitle.message: Browser sync where your data stays genuinely yours. Your bookmarks, sessions and extensions go straight to storage you own. No server in between.

onb_feature_storage.message: Your data always stays on storage you own.

onb_feature_instant.message: Syncs every change as it happens.

onb_feature_browsers.message: Works in Chromium and Firefox based browsers.

onb_feature_providers.message: You decide where your data lives.

onb_backend_subtitle.message: Where should Kesonode store your data?

onb_use_provider.description: Accessible name of a storage-provider card. $PROVIDER$ is a brand name and is never translated.

opt_use_provider.description: Accessible name of a storage card in Settings, as in the setup wizard. $PROVIDER$ is a brand name and is never translated.

opt_provider_active.description: Badge on the storage card that is saved and in use. Shown in capitals.

opt_drive_disconnect.description: Button on the Google Drive card: this device forgets its Google sign-in. Nothing in Drive is deleted.

opt_drive_unavailable.message: Google sign-in isn't available in this browser. Pick another option.
opt_drive_unavailable.description: On the Google Drive card in Settings, on a browser with no way to sign in to Google (Firefox for Android has no identity API). The same sentence as setup's.

provider_webdav_other.description: Name of the storage card for any other WebDAV server. WebDAV is not translated, only the word in brackets.

onb_drive_unavailable.message: Google sign-in isn't available in this browser. Pick another option.

onb_signin_failed.description: Last-resort text when the sign-in threw something with no message of its own.

onb_github_401.message: GitHub rejected this token. Check it hasn't expired, and that you pasted all of it.

onb_github_unreachable.message: Couldn't reach GitHub. Check your connection and try again.

onb_github_token_link.message: Create a fine-grained token (only this repo) →

onb_data_subtitle.message: You can change this anytime in Settings.

onb_device_name_desc.message: How it appears in the session list on your other devices.

onb_device_name_placeholder.description: An example name, not a default. The field arrives pre-filled with the detected one.

onb_encrypt_subtitle.message: If you turn encryption on, your data is encrypted on this device before it is uploaded. Not even your storage provider can read what it contains.

onb_e2ee_desc.message: AES-256-GCM. If you turn this on, keep the passphrase safe — it cannot be recovered.

onb_pass_placeholder.message: Choose a passphrase, or generate an encryption key

onb_pass_missing.message: Enter a passphrase, or generate a key.

onb_pass_too_short.message: At least $MIN$ characters. Synced data can be attacked offline, so short passphrases are guessable.

onb_save_passphrase_lead.description: Shown in bold, immediately before onb_save_passphrase_rest. One sentence on its own.

onb_save_passphrase_rest.message: It never leaves this device and cannot be recovered if you lose it. You have to enter the same passphrase on every device. You can copy it later in Settings.

onb_plaintext_note.message: Without encryption, your data goes to your own storage $WORD$. That can be the right choice if you fully trust your storage provider. You can turn encryption on later in Settings at any time.
onb_plaintext_note.description: $WORD$ is onb_plaintext_word, shown in bold inside this sentence, so the sentence is split at the placeholder.

onb_plaintext_word.description: The bold word dropped into onb_plaintext_note. Lower case: it sits mid-sentence.

onb_waiting_permission.description: The Finish & Sync button while the browser's permission prompt is open.

onb_perm_prompt_slow.message: No permission prompt on screen? Some browsers don't show one. Allow Kesonode's permissions in your browser's extension settings and press Finish & Sync again, or go back and turn off the data types that need them.
onb_perm_prompt_slow.description: Shown under Finish & Sync when the permission prompt has gone unanswered for several seconds, because some browsers never show it. Name the button as it reads in your translation.

onb_err_bad_webdav_url.message: That WebDAV address doesn't look like a valid URL.

onb_err_perms_webdav.message: Kesonode needs permission to reach your WebDAV server and the data types you chose. Please allow them to continue.

onb_err_perms_no_prompt.message: This browser can't show permission prompts, so Kesonode couldn't ask for the access it needs. Grant it on Kesonode's permissions screen in your browser's extension settings, then press Finish again.

onb_err_perms_types.message: Some permissions were declined. Grant them, or turn off those data types, to continue.

onb_err_read_settings.message: Couldn't read your current settings. Try again.

onb_err_save.description: $ERROR$ is a message from the engine and stays in English. See CLAUDE.md on why the diagnostic layer is not translated.

onb_direction_subtitle.message: Your other devices already have bookmarks in this storage. Decide which side wins before anything is merged or published — this question is asked once.

onb_direction_hint.message: Not sure? Nothing is merged until you choose — you can close this; the Kesonode popup will remind you to finish choosing.

onb_sync_subtitle.message: Kesonode is running its first sync. This also runs in the background, so you don't have to wait here.

onb_sync_error_subtitle.message: Your settings are saved. Open Settings to fix this, or finish and let Kesonode retry in the background.

onb_sync_timeout.message: This is taking longer than usual. A large history can do that. The sync keeps running in the background, so you can finish now.

onb_done_subtitle.message: Kesonode is now syncing your browser data to $BACKEND$. The first sync is already running in the background.
onb_done_subtitle.description: $BACKEND$ is shown in bold and is a brand name, so the sentence is split at the placeholder.

datatype_bookmarks_desc.message: Full bookmark tree with folders and ordering.
datatype_bookmarks_desc.description: Shown under the data type on BOTH the setup wizard and Settings. The two screens used to carry different wording and drifted apart.

datatype_sessions_desc.message: Named tab sessions you can restore anywhere.
datatype_sessions_desc.description: Deliberately not 'tab groups': that names a Chrome feature Kesonode does not sync, which the setup wizard used to claim.

datatype_history_desc.message: Browsing history, limited by the days setting.
datatype_history_desc.description: Not a fixed number of days: the setup wizard used to promise 'Last 30 days' while the limit is adjustable in Settings.

datatype_extensions_desc.message: Extension list, showing missing ones with install links.

opt_secret_copy.description: Tooltip on the button that copies a saved secret (token, password, passphrase) to the clipboard.

opt_secret_copied.description: Replaces opt_secret_copy for a moment after the copy succeeded.

opt_secret_replace.description: Tooltip on the button that clears a saved secret so a new one can be typed. Kesonode never shows a saved secret in an editable field, so replacing is the only way to change it.

opt_webdav_user_placeholder.description: Greyed-out example inside the empty username field. Lowercase on purpose, so it reads as an example rather than a filled-in value.

opt_webdav_pass_label.description: Most WebDAV servers want an app-specific token here rather than the account password, which is why both words appear.

opt_webdav_http_warn.message: Kesonode does not connect over $SCHEME$: credentials would travel in the clear. Use https://, or http:// only on this computer.
opt_webdav_http_warn.description: Warning under a WebDAV card whose address is refused. $SCHEME$ is rendered as code and is never translated. Split around the placeholder with tParts, so word order stays yours.

opt_webdav_http_use.description: Follows opt_webdav_http_warn. $SCHEME$ is rendered as code and is never translated.

opt_snap_restored_one.message: Restored $COUNT$ bookmark. Syncing to your other devices…
opt_snap_restored_one.description: A restore only ever ADDS bookmarks back, so this number is what was re-added, never what was removed.

opt_snap_restored_other.message: Restored $COUNT$ bookmarks. Syncing to your other devices…
opt_snap_restored_other.description: Plural form of opt_snap_restored_one. Hungarian keeps the singular after a numeral, so both forms are worded the same there.

opt_err_perms_no_prompt.message: This browser can't show permission prompts, so Kesonode couldn't ask for access to your WebDAV server. Grant it on Kesonode's permissions screen in your browser's extension settings, then try again.
opt_err_perms_no_prompt.description: Firefox for Android implements no runtime permission prompts. Saying 'you declined' there would blame the user for something they were never asked.

opt_err_perms_bad_url.message: Kesonode has no usable WebDAV address to ask for access to. Check the server URL above.

opt_err_perms_denied.message: Permission to access the WebDAV server was not granted.

opt_err_pass_too_short.message: Use at least $MIN$ characters. Synced data can be attacked offline, so a short passphrase is guessable. Longer is better, or generate a key.
opt_err_pass_too_short.description: Settings' version of onb_pass_too_short. Longer than the onboarding one because here there is room to say what to do about it.

opt_err_pass_mismatch.message: The two passphrases don't match. Re-enter to confirm before saving.

opt_saved.description: Shown on the Save button for a moment after a write the extension actually confirmed. Never shown for a write that failed.

opt_nav_backend.description: Tab in the Settings navigation strip. Keep every nav label short: the strip has to stay legible when the window is narrow. The section heading is a separate key (opt_backend_head), so you can be shorter here than there.

opt_nav_data.description: Tab in the Settings navigation strip. Keep it short, see opt_nav_backend.

opt_nav_device.description: Tab in the Settings navigation strip. Keep it short, see opt_nav_backend.

opt_nav_activity.description: Tab in the Settings navigation strip. Keep it short, see opt_nav_backend.

opt_nav_advanced.description: Tab in the Settings navigation strip. Keep it short, see opt_nav_backend.

opt_setup_title.description: Card shown at the top of Settings until first-run setup is complete.

opt_setup_step_storage.message: Choose where your data is stored

opt_backend_head.description: Heading of the Storage section. Separate from the nav label opt_nav_backend, which has to fit a narrow strip, so this one can be as long as it needs to be.

opt_backend_head_sub.message: Choose where your sync data is stored. Your data never touches our servers.

opt_gdrive_connect_failed.description: Fallback when Google sign-in throws without a message of its own.

opt_gdrive_scope_hint.message: Only the $SCOPE$ scope, so Kesonode can only access files it creates.
opt_gdrive_scope_hint.description: $SCOPE$ is the OAuth scope name drive.file, rendered as code and never translated. Split around the placeholder with tParts.

opt_optional.description: Appended to a field label the user can leave empty. Keep the parentheses.

opt_drive_folder_placeholder.message: Leave blank to auto-create the sync folder
opt_drive_folder_placeholder.description: The folder's fixed name is protocol data, explained under Advanced → Compatibility. Do not put the upstream product name in this placeholder.

opt_compat_folder_desc.message: The name on the right follows the mode. `konode` (`Konode` on Google Drive) is the frozen upstream name; `kesonode` (`Kesonode` on Drive) starts a separate sync group.

opt_github_token_label.description: GitHub's own name for this credential. If GitHub's interface uses a translated name in your language, match it.

opt_github_branch_label.description: The git branch. Most languages keep the English word here; use whatever git's own interface uses in yours.

opt_stat_never.description: Value of the 'Last sync' tile when this device has never completed a sync.

opt_setup_sub.message: Kesonode syncs your browser to storage you own. There's no Kesonode server. Two quick steps and you're done. (If the setup wizard never opened on your browser, you can do everything right here.)

opt_data_head.description: Heading of the Data Types tab. Separate from the nav label opt_nav_data, which has to fit a narrow strip.

opt_data_head_sub.message: Choose what gets synced across your devices.

opt_data_permission_lost.message: Kesonode doesn't have the permission this needs any more, so it isn't syncing. Switch it off and on again to restore it.
opt_data_permission_lost.description: A browser can revoke an optional permission from its own extension settings without telling the extension, which leaves a data type looking enabled while it syncs nothing.

opt_tab_groups_desc.message: Open tabs come back in their groups either way. With this on, the groups keep their names and colours as well.

opt_tab_groups_denied.message: Kesonode needs the "tabGroups" permission for this. Your groups still come back, without names.

opt_history_days_value.description: The slider's current value, in a narrow space beside it. Abbreviate the unit if your language can; there is not much room.

opt_history_hint.message: Pages from your other devices are added with the time they arrived, not the time you first visited them, so on Chromium browsers they show up under today rather than the day you were browsing. Firefox keeps the original date.
opt_history_hint.description: Chrome's history.addUrl takes no visit time; Firefox's does and Kesonode passes it. Without this note a working sync looks broken.

opt_missing_ext_head.description: Heading over the list of extensions your other devices have and this one does not.

opt_ext_from.description: Which store a missing extension can be installed from. $STORE$ is a store's brand name (Chrome Web Store or Firefox Add-ons) and is never translated. Naming the store in full is deliberate: this line sits near a list of devices, and a bare 'Chrome' was read as one. Keep the leading middle dot, it separates this from the extension's name.

opt_ext_install.description: Link on a missing extension that exists in THIS browser's store, so it can be installed directly.

opt_ext_find.description: Replaces opt_ext_install when the extension came from the other browser's store: extension IDs don't cross stores, so the link can only run a name search.

opt_no_password_body.message: Browser extensions cannot access the native password store.
opt_no_password_body.description: A deliberate security boundary in the browser, not a Kesonode limitation.

opt_no_password_use.description: $MANAGERS$ is rendered as two product links joined by opt_or, so it is never translated. Split around the placeholder with tParts.

opt_or.description: Joins two alternatives that are each their own link, so they cannot be part of one translatable sentence.

opt_device_head.description: Heading of the Device tab. Separate from the nav label opt_nav_device, which has to fit a narrow strip.

opt_device_head_sub.message: Identify this device in the sync network.

opt_device_name_desc.message: How this device appears in sync logs and on your other devices. Browsers do not let extensions read the computer's own name, so set it yourself (e.g. Mac mini M4pro).

opt_device_name_placeholder.description: Example device name in the empty field. Use something ordinary in your language, it is only an example.

opt_device_id_desc.description: Every synced file is named after this id, so a new one would orphan the old files.

opt_sync_on_change_desc.message: Instantly sync bookmarks when they change. Recommended.

opt_auto_sync_desc.message: Also sync on a regular schedule. History, open tabs and the extension list travel only this way.

opt_interval_desc.message: How often this device pulls remote changes. 30s is the browser's minimum for background checks. Your own changes upload almost instantly.

opt_interval_value.description: The interval slider's current value in seconds, in a narrow space beside it. Abbreviate the unit if your language can.

opt_conflict_lww_desc.message: The newest change wins. A bookmark deleted on another device is deleted here too, unless you added it again after it was deleted there.
opt_conflict_lww_desc.description: Under 'Last Write Wins' in Settings → Device → Conflict resolution. Each of the four options says what it does with bookmarks another device deletes, because that is where they differ most.

opt_conflict_local_desc.message: This device's bookmarks win. New bookmarks from other devices still arrive, but their deletions, moves and renames are never applied here.
opt_conflict_local_desc.description: Under 'Prefer Local'. The important promise is that deletions made on other devices never remove anything on this device.

opt_conflict_remote_desc.message: Other devices' moves and renames win over yours. Their deletions are applied the same way as Last Write Wins.
opt_conflict_remote_desc.description: Under 'Prefer Remote'. 'Last Write Wins' is the name of the first option (opt_conflict_lww), so use the same translation for it here.

opt_conflict_manual_desc.message: Ask me in the popup when this device and another one differ. Until you choose that device's version, none of its bookmark changes are applied here, deletions included.
opt_conflict_manual_desc.description: Under 'Manual'. The popup shows a card per device with 'Keep local' and 'Use remote'; 'choose that device's version' means 'Use remote'.

opt_bulk_delete_label.message: Max bulk delete from a peer

opt_bulk_delete_desc.message: A safety net: if a peer's deletions would remove more than this share of your local bookmarks, the merge skips them (guards against a corrupt sync wiping your tree). Raise it if you routinely delete in bulk.

opt_baseline_label.description: Section heading in Settings → Device and the status label in Activity. Names the browser whose bookmarks the group was aligned to.

opt_baseline_desc.message: The browser whose bookmarks the group was aligned to. Other browsers apply it once, then merge both ways again.
opt_baseline_desc.description: Explains the bookmark baseline. The setting applies immediately, not through the Save button.

opt_baseline_none.message: Not set — bookmarks merge in both directions.

opt_baseline_unavailable.message: Couldn't read the baseline from the storage.

opt_baseline_stale.message: · the storage no longer holds this marker (it may have been cleared, or never written)

opt_baseline_waiting.message: This browser hasn't aligned with $DEVICE$ yet; it will on the next sync.

opt_baseline_confirm_set.message: Other browsers will replace their bookmarks with this browser's copy once. Each one saves its own restore point first, and sync is two-way again afterwards.
opt_baseline_confirm_set.description: Confirmation shown before this browser becomes the baseline. It replaces other browsers' bookmark trees once; each of them saves its own restore point first.

opt_baseline_confirm_clear.message: Bookmarks stay as they are on every browser, and sync becomes two-way again.
opt_baseline_confirm_clear.description: Confirmation before removing the baseline. No bookmarks are deleted.

opt_baseline_set_confirm.description: Confirm button in the Bookmark baseline card. Distinct from the label that opens the confirmation, so the second, committing click is unmistakable.

opt_baseline_clear_confirm.description: Confirm button for removing the baseline.

opt_baseline_save_pending.message: The bookmark baseline was not changed: the confirmation is still open in the card above. Click its confirm button — the change takes effect immediately, and "Save changes" does not apply to it.
opt_baseline_save_pending.description: Shown in the baseline card when Save changes is pressed while a baseline confirmation is still open.

opt_baseline_set_done.message: This browser is now the baseline. Other browsers will align on their next sync.

opt_baseline_cleared.message: Baseline cleared. Bookmarks merge both ways again.

bm_exclude_label.description: The switch, under Bookmarks in Settings and in the setup wizard, that opens a tree of this browser's bookmarks for picking what stays out of sync.

bm_exclude_desc.message: Tick the folders and bookmarks this device keeps to itself. They stay here untouched, and nothing your other devices do changes them.

bm_exclude_hint.message: Excluding something deletes nothing: copies your other devices already have stay there. Moving a bookmark into an excluded folder later removes it from your other devices, as if you had deleted it.
bm_exclude_hint.description: Shown under the bookmark tree in Settings.

bm_exclude_loading.description: Shown while the bookmark tree is being read.

bm_exclude_error.description: The browser refused to hand over the bookmark tree. $ERROR$ is its own message, usually English.

bm_exclude_empty.message: There are no bookmarks on this device yet.
bm_exclude_empty.description: Shown instead of the tree when there are no bookmarks at all.

bm_exclude_untitled.description: A folder with no name, in the bookmark tree.

bm_exclude_expand.description: Screen-reader label of the arrow that opens a folder in the bookmark tree.

bm_exclude_collapse.description: Screen-reader label of the arrow that closes a folder in the bookmark tree.

bm_exclude_count_one.description: How many bookmarks a folder holds, beside it in the tree, in the case of exactly one.

bm_exclude_count_other.description: How many bookmarks a folder holds, beside it in the tree. In languages that use the singular after a numeral, this is the same wording as the _one form.

bm_exclude_more_one.description: A button at the end of a long folder in the bookmark tree, showing the next entries.

bm_exclude_more_other.description: A button at the end of a long folder in the bookmark tree, showing the next entries.

bm_list_more_one.description: Under a short list of bookmarks, for the ones not listed. Shown under the bookmarks a blocked deletion would remove, in Settings → Activity. Starts lowercase because it continues the list.

opt_conflicts_section.description: Card in Settings → Activity, shown only while Manual conflict resolution is waiting for an answer. The popup's Resolve button leads here.

opt_conflicts_section_sub.message: This device and another one hold different versions. Conflict resolution is set to Manual, so Kesonode waits for you to choose.
opt_conflicts_section_sub.description: Sub-heading under 'Conflicts'. 'Manual' is the conflict resolution option of that name (opt_conflict_manual).

opt_conflicts_explain.message: “$KEEP$” leaves this device as it is. “$REMOTE$” merges the other device's changes into this one.
opt_conflicts_explain.description: What the two buttons do. $KEEP$ and $REMOTE$ are the buttons' own labels (popup_keep_local, popup_use_remote), filled in by the code.

opt_conflict_bookmarks.description: Heading of one conflict. $DEVICE$ is the other device's name, which the user chose.

opt_conflict_history.description: Heading of one conflict. $DEVICE$ is the other device's name, which the user chose.

opt_diff_loading.description: Shown while the two versions are being compared. With encryption on this can take a few seconds.

opt_diff_failed.description: Shown if the comparison gave no usable answer.

opt_diff_only_remote.description: Above a list of bookmarks or visited pages that the other device has and this one does not. $DEVICE$ is that device's name, $COUNT$ how many there are.

opt_diff_only_local.description: Above a list of bookmarks or visited pages that this device has and the other one does not. $COUNT$ is how many there are.

opt_diff_changed_one.message: $COUNT$ bookmark is on both, under a different title or in a different folder.
opt_diff_changed_one.description: Bookmarks with the same address on both devices, but renamed or in a different folder on one of them.

opt_diff_changed_other.message: $COUNT$ bookmarks are on both, under a different title or in a different folder.

opt_diff_none_bookmarks.message: Both devices have the same bookmarks now.
opt_diff_none_bookmarks.description: Shown instead of the lists when nothing differs any more between the two devices' bookmarks.

opt_diff_none_history.message: Both devices visited the same pages. Only the visit times or counts differ.
opt_diff_none_history.description: Shown instead of the lists when both devices visited the same pages and only the visit details differ.

bm_exclude_summary_one.description: Under the bookmark tree: how many folders and bookmarks are ticked, in the case of exactly one.

bm_exclude_summary_other.description: Under the bookmark tree: how many folders and bookmarks are ticked.

bm_exclude_none.description: Under the bookmark tree, when nothing is ticked.

opt_activity_head.description: Heading of the Activity tab. Separate from the nav label opt_nav_activity, which has to fit a narrow strip.

opt_activity_head_sub.message: What Kesonode did on this device, and what it has to work with. All computed here: the numbers, the restore points and the last 200 log entries are local and nothing on this page is ever uploaded.

opt_status_paused_hint.message: Automatic sync is waiting out the storage's rate-limit window (or a repeated failure). Press Sync now in the popup to retry immediately.

opt_status_totals_hint.message: How many items of each type this device synced last: bookmarks as links, history within the configured window, extensions installed here, and sessions as other devices' sessions you can restore.

opt_devices_section_sub.message: Every device with files in your sync folder, and what each one last uploaded. Forgetting a device deletes its files from your storage. It removes no bookmarks from any browser.

opt_forget_result_one.message: Deleted one file belonging to $LABEL$. If that browser is still running, it will upload itself again within a minute and reappear here. That is not a fault: to keep a device out, turn Kesonode off there first, then forget it here.
opt_forget_result_one.description: $LABEL$ is the device's own name, so it is never translated. $COUNT$ is available as the second substitution but this form does not need it.

opt_forget_result_other.message: Deleted $COUNT$ files belonging to $LABEL$. If that browser is still running, it will upload itself again within a minute and reappear here. That is not a fault: to keep a device out, turn Kesonode off there first, then forget it here.
opt_forget_result_other.description: Plural of opt_forget_result_one. $LABEL$ is the device's own name and is never translated.

opt_devices_error.message: Couldn't read your devices: $ERROR$. This does not mean you have none.
opt_devices_error.description: An empty list must never stand in for a list that failed to load. $ERROR$ is the technical message and is not translated.

opt_error_check_connection.message: Check the connection in Storage and reopen this tab.
opt_error_check_connection.description: Follows the device-list and restore-point errors when the error itself gives no advice. Left out after the lost-permission message, which already says to open Settings → Storage and press Save. 'Storage' names the tab, so it must match the tab's own translation.

opt_devices_empty.message: Nothing in the folder yet. Run a sync and this device will appear.

opt_device_unnamed.description: Shown when every packet Kesonode could read for a device came from a build that carried no name. $ID$ is the start of the device id.

opt_this_device.description: Badge marking your own device in the list. Upper case matches the other badges; use whatever reads as a badge in your language.

opt_last_upload_ago.description: Follows the list of data types on a device row. $WHEN$ is how long ago, already worded by the browser in your language, such as "39 days ago", "3 hours ago" or "2 years ago", so build the phrase around a time of that shape. Keep the leading middle dot, it separates this from the types.

opt_device_browser.description: The browser a device runs and the engine it is built on, shown after the device's name, for example "Brave (Chromium)" or "Firefox (Gecko)". Both are product names and are never translated. Change only the punctuation, if your language writes brackets differently.

opt_device_dormant.description: Badge on a device in the list that has uploaded nothing for a long time (the line under it says how long). Calm, not alarming: nothing is wrong and nothing happens to the device. Upper case matches the other badges; use whatever reads as a badge in your language.

opt_device_dormant_note_one.message: Nothing uploaded in over a day. That can mean nothing changed there, or that this browser is gone. If it is gone, you can forget it.
opt_device_dormant_note_one.description: Under a device marked INACTIVE. A device uploads only when something it syncs has changed, so a long silence is not proof the device is gone, and this says both. "Forget" is the button on the same row. $COUNT$ is available but this form does not need it.

opt_device_dormant_note_other.message: Nothing uploaded in over $COUNT$ days. That can mean nothing changed there, or that this browser is gone. If it is gone, you can forget it.
opt_device_dormant_note_other.description: Plural of opt_device_dormant_note_one. $COUNT$ is a number of days, 30 today.

opt_forget.description: Button that deletes a device's files from your storage. Deliberately not a bin icon: what goes is a few files in your own folder, not anybody's bookmarks.

opt_forget_confirm_one.message: Deletes the one file this device has in your storage ($TYPES$). No bookmarks are removed from any browser, here or there. If that browser is still running it will upload itself again and reappear; to keep it out, turn Kesonode off there first.
opt_forget_confirm_one.description: $TYPES$ is the list of data types, already translated elsewhere and joined with commas.

opt_forget_confirm_other.message: Deletes the $COUNT$ files this device has in your storage ($TYPES$). No bookmarks are removed from any browser, here or there. If that browser is still running it will upload itself again and reappear; to keep it out, turn Kesonode off there first.

opt_that_device.description: Stands in for a device's name in opt_forget_result_* when the device never published one.

opt_blocked_section.description: Card in Settings → Activity, shown only while the mass-delete guard is holding a peer's deletion back. This is where the popup banner sends people.

opt_blocked_section_sub.message: Another device asked to remove an unusual number of your bookmarks, so Kesonode held it back. Apply it if you meant to, or keep them.
opt_blocked_section_sub.description: Sub-heading under 'Blocked deletion'. Says what happened and that there is a choice to make.

opt_blocked_headline_one.description: How big the blocked deletion is. The proportion is the whole point, so both numbers stay in the sentence.

opt_blocked_count_one.description: Fallback headline for a notice saved by an older version, which recorded the count but not the size of the tree.

opt_blocked_from.description: Names the peer device that sent the deletion. $DEVICE$ is a name the user chose.

opt_blocked_from_unknown.description: Used when the peer's packet carries no device name (older builds did not send one).

opt_blocked_saved.message: Nothing was removed, and a restore point was saved first.
opt_blocked_saved.description: The reassurance. Sits right after opt_blocked_from in the same paragraph.

opt_blocked_recent_one.message: Other devices already removed $COUNT$ bookmark here in the last 24 hours, and this would take the total past your bulk-delete limit.
opt_blocked_recent_one.description: Under the blocked-deletion headline, only when earlier deletions from other devices are why a deletion smaller than the limit was held back: the guard adds up what peers removed here over a day (#41). The limit is the 'Max bulk delete from a peer' setting.

opt_blocked_recent_other.message: Other devices already removed $COUNT$ bookmarks here in the last 24 hours, and this would take the total past your bulk-delete limit.

opt_blocked_apply.description: Button. First step of two, because applying removes bookmarks.

opt_blocked_confirm_apply.description: The confirming second click. Deliberately says the word delete.

opt_blocked_keep.message: To keep them instead, restore a point from before the cleanup on the device that asked. That clears its record of the deletion, so it stops being sent here.
opt_blocked_keep.description: The other way out, which has to happen on the OTHER device. Worth stating because there is nothing on this device that can stop the asking.

opt_snapshots_section_sub.message: Timestamped copies of your bookmarks on the backend, shared by all your devices. Restoring adds back any bookmarks missing on this device (it never deletes). The newest 10 automatic points are kept, and the points you save by hand get 10 slots of their own; older ones are removed automatically. A point you keep forever is never removed.

opt_snap_now_desc.message: A restore point of your current bookmark tree.

opt_snap_error_desc.message: This does not mean you have none. They live on your storage and could not be listed just now.
opt_snap_error_desc.description: On a recovery screen, 'you have no backups' is the worst possible thing to say by mistake.

opt_snap_empty.message: No restore points yet. Create one above, or one is saved automatically if an unusual deletion is ever blocked.

opt_snap_partial.message: The storage can't be listed right now (most likely a rate-limit window), so this shows only the restore points this device already knows about. Points made on other devices will appear once it answers again — nothing has been deleted.

opt_snap_count_other.description: Plural of opt_snap_count_one. Hungarian and German keep the same noun form here.

opt_snap_unknown.description: Used instead of a count when the shared index could not be read, for instance before a passphrase is set. A bare 'bookmarks' with no number reads as a rendering fault.

opt_snap_create_kept.message: Create a restore point kept forever

opt_log_errors.description: Appended after opt_log_count_*. Keep the leading space and middle dot, they separate it from what came before.

opt_log_skipped.description: Appended after opt_log_count_* and opt_log_errors. Keep the leading space and middle dot.

opt_log_copy_label.description: Row label next to the Copy log button in Settings → Activity.

opt_log_copy_desc.message: Word for word, oldest first, with the Kesonode version and your browser. That includes your storage server's address and those of pages Kesonode couldn't sync, so read it before posting it anywhere public.
opt_log_copy_desc.description: Says the copy is not redacted, and why that matters. The log lines themselves stay in English on purpose.

opt_log_copy.description: Button. Puts the whole Activity log on the clipboard as text.

opt_log_copy_failed.message: This browser wouldn't let Kesonode copy the log. Select the entries below and copy them by hand.
opt_log_copy_failed.description: Shown when the clipboard refuses the copy.

opt_log_nothing.message: Nothing logged yet. Run a sync and it'll show up here.

opt_e2ee_desc.message: AES-256-GCM. Data is encrypted with your passphrase before it leaves this device, so the storage provider can never read it. Keep the passphrase safe: without it, encrypted data can't be recovered, and every device must use the same one.

opt_e2ee_disable_confirm.message: Turn off encryption? Your synced data will be stored $UNENCRYPTED$ on your backend from the next sync on. Every device must then also turn it off.
opt_e2ee_disable_confirm.description: $UNENCRYPTED$ is opt_unencrypted, rendered bold. Split around the placeholder with tParts. Turning E2EE off is a downgrade, which is why it asks.

opt_unencrypted.description: Rendered bold inside opt_e2ee_disable_confirm and opt_e2ee_off_warning. It is the word carrying the warning, which is why it is emphasised.

opt_passphrase_desc.message: Derives the encryption key. Stored only on this device, never uploaded.

opt_genkey_saved_warning.message: Save this now. It's the only way to recover your data if you forget it. Enter the same key on your other devices.

opt_e2ee_no_passphrase.message: Encryption is on but no passphrase is set, so sync keeps uploading plaintext until you add one.

opt_e2ee_off_warning.message: Encryption is off, so your synced data (bookmarks, history, sessions, extensions) is stored $UNENCRYPTED$ on your backend. Turn it on to encrypt everything before it leaves this device.
opt_e2ee_off_warning.description: $UNENCRYPTED$ is opt_unencrypted, rendered bold. Split around the placeholder with tParts.

opt_advanced_head.description: Heading of the Advanced tab. Separate from the nav label opt_nav_advanced, which has to fit a narrow strip.

opt_export_desc.message: Download bookmarks, history, and extensions as a JSON file. No cloud needed.

opt_import_desc.message: Restore from a Kesonode JSON backup. Bookmarks added to a new folder.

opt_import_ok_one.description: $FOLDER$ is the folder name the import creates. It is data shared across devices, so it is never translated.

opt_import_ok_other.description: Plural of opt_import_ok_one. $FOLDER$ is never translated.

opt_cfg_export_desc.message: Save your configuration — storage providers, folders, schedules, preferences and device ID — as a JSON file. Sign-in credentials are left out unless you choose to include them, and then the file is encrypted with a password you set.

opt_cfg_export_include_desc.message: Adds the WebDAV password, GitHub token, Google Drive session and E2EE passphrase, encrypted with the password below. Without them the file restores your settings but you sign in again afterwards.

opt_cfg_export_password_note.message: There is no way to recover this file without the password. Keep both somewhere private.

opt_cfg_export_pw_mismatch.message: The two passwords do not match.

opt_cfg_import_desc.message: Restore your configuration after an upgrade instead of setting everything up again. Replaces the current settings. If the file is encrypted, you will be asked for its password.

opt_cfg_import_pw_desc.message: Enter the password you set when exporting it to open the file.

opt_cfg_import_pass_label.message: This backup needs your encryption passphrase

opt_cfg_import_pass_desc.message: The backup enables end-to-end encryption but carries no passphrase. Enter the one this device should use — without it the import cannot be completed (and uploading in plaintext is not an option).

opt_cfg_import_pass_short.message: The passphrase must be at least $LEN$ characters.

opt_cfg_import_missing.message: The backup carried no sign-in credentials, so syncing cannot start until you sign in to: $ACCOUNTS$. Open Settings → Storage, enter them and save.

opt_cfg_import_auth.message: The imported config points at the WebDAV server $HOST$, but Kesonode has no permission to reach it yet. Grant access now, or syncing will fail with "Failed to fetch".

opt_cfg_import_auth_err.message: The browser refused the request. Grant the host permission for $HOST$ from your browser's extension settings, then sync again.

opt_feedback_section_sub.message: Nothing is sent automatically. These just open when you click them.

opt_report_label.message: Report a bug or request a feature

opt_report_desc.message: Opens the project's GitHub issues (public, tied to your GitHub account).

opt_email_desc.message: For anything you'd rather not post publicly.

opt_rate_desc.message: If Kesonode works for you, a rating helps other people find it (public, tied to your store account).

opt_debug_desc.message: Verbose logging, to the browser console and to Activity so you can share it. Turn it off when you're done.

opt_devices_bad_reply.description: Reported through opt_devices_error when the extension replies in a shape the page did not expect. An empty list must never stand in for a list that failed to load.

onb_import_desc.message: Import a configuration backup you exported earlier to restore sync settings without filling in the wizard again.

onb_import_button.message: Choose a backup file and import

onb_import_done_desc.message: Your sync settings are restored. If this version needs new permissions, grant them in the next step.

onb_perm_desc.message: Kesonode needs these permissions for the setup you chose. Grant them and sync continues.

onb_perm_denied.message: Permission was not granted. You can allow it in the browser's extension settings, or try again.

import_confirm_overwrite.message: Import this configuration file? It will overwrite your current settings.

import_confirm_new_device.message:
Is this backup from another device or browser?

[OK] Import as a new device: generate a fresh device ID and default name (recommended)
[Cancel] Restore this machine's identity: keep the backup's device ID and name (for an upgrade or reinstall of the same machine)

import_risk_header.message:
This file will make the following sensitive changes:
$LIST$

Import it anyway?

import_risk_disables_e2ee.message: Turns off end-to-end encryption (data is then uploaded in plaintext)

import_risk_changes_backend.message: Changes the sync backend (it may point at another server)

import_risk_has_credentials.message: Contains plaintext backend credentials (WebDAV password / GitHub token)

import_risk_has_gdrive_session.message: Contains a Google Drive sign-in token

opt_first_sync_merge_desc.message: Keep the bookmarks in this browser and add those from the other devices. The result is the union of both; nothing is deleted.

opt_first_sync_remote_desc.message: Clear the bookmarks in this browser and rebuild them from the newest other device. A restore point is saved first, but bookmarks that exist only here are lost.

opt_first_sync_local.message: Use this browser as the baseline

opt_first_sync_local_desc.message: Other browsers replace their bookmarks with this browser's copy once, each saving its own restore point first. Sync is two-way again afterwards, so changes made later on any browser still arrive everywhere.

popup_first_sync_notice.message: First sync: choose how to combine bookmarks

onb_step_progress.description: Progress line above the setup wizard. $CURRENT$ is the step number, $TOTAL$ how many steps there are.

onb_later.description: Quiet link in the wizard header that closes the tab. The half-filled setup is kept for a day and can be resumed from the toolbar popup.

onb_err_no_types.message: Pick at least one thing to sync — with all of them off, Kesonode has nothing to do.
onb_err_no_types.description: Shown on the 'What to sync?' step when every switch is off, so Continue is disabled.

onb_perm_upcoming.description: Lead-in above the list of permissions the Finish button is about to request from the browser.

perm_host_label.description: Name of a host permission in a permission list. The address itself (https://host/*) is printed under it, untranslated.

perm_denied_note.message: If you decline, that data type stops syncing. Everything else keeps working.
perm_denied_note.description: What happens if the user declines an optional permission. Reassures that the rest keeps working.

onb_manage_title.description: Heading of the page shown when someone opens onboarding.html on an install that is already set up.

onb_manage_sub.message: This page only shows the current setup. Change it in Settings, or run the wizard again.
onb_manage_sub.description: Explains that this page is read-only and where to change things instead.

onb_manage_perms_label.description: Row label in the summary of an existing setup: whether the permissions it needs are granted.

onb_manage_perms_ok.description: Value in the permissions row when nothing is missing.

onb_manage_perms_missing.description: Value in the permissions row when some are missing. $COUNT$ is how many.

onb_manage_reconfigure.description: Button that deliberately re-enters the setup wizard. It replaces the stored configuration when finished, so it is confirmed first.

onb_manage_reconfigure_confirm.message: Run setup again? Finishing the wizard replaces your storage, your sync choices and your device name.
onb_manage_reconfigure_confirm.description: Confirmation dialog before re-running setup. Says exactly what will be replaced, because finishing the wizard overwrites it.

onb_done_summary.description: Heading over the per-data-type counts on the final screen, so the page reports what happened instead of three fixed ticks.

onb_done_multi_title.description: Heading of the second-device hint on the final screen. A sync extension does nothing until a second browser joins.

onb_done_multi_body.message: Install Kesonode there and pick the same storage. Bookmarks, tabs and the rest will meet in the middle.
onb_done_multi_body.description: Tells the user what to do on the next browser: install, then pick the same storage.

popup_receipt_danger.message: The last sync removed $REMOVED$ bookmarks. A restore point was saved.

popup_search_placeholder.message: Search bookmarks, history and reading list

popup_reading_error.message: Couldn't load your reading list: $ERROR$. This does not mean it is empty.
popup_reading_error.description: An empty list must never stand in for a list that failed to load. $ERROR$ is the technical message and is not translated.

popup_reading_no_tab.message: This tab has no address to save.

opt_receipt_section_sub.message: What the last completed cycle changed on this device.

opt_receipt_danger.message: This cycle removed a large share of this device's bookmarks. A restore point was saved before the merge.

opt_receipt_undo_desc.message: Restore the bookmark tree saved just before these changes were applied.

opt_conflict_types_section_sub.message: Leave a type on Follow the setting above unless it needs its own answer.

opt_cleanup_section_sub.message: Find duplicate URLs, and optionally links that no longer answer.

opt_cleanup_scan_desc.message: Duplicates are found from this browser's tree. Nothing is removed until you choose the rows and confirm.

opt_cleanup_dead_desc.message: Runs one network request per bookmarked host, up to 300 links per run. Only 404/410 count as dead; timeouts and login walls are left alone. Off by default because it contacts sites from this device.

opt_cleanup_dead_cap.message: Checked $PROBED$ links this run; the rest wait for the next run.

opt_cleanup_none.message: No duplicates or dead links found.

opt_auto_snapshot_desc.message: When a merge would remove a large share of this device's bookmarks, a restore point is saved first and offered as Undo on Activity.

opt_order_desc.message: Whether a peer's folder position moves your copy (newest wins), or this browser keeps its own order.

opt_autosave_section_sub.message: Open tabs kept on this device between syncs, so a crash or a closed window leaves a way back.

opt_autosave_enable_desc.message: Saved after a session sync and never uploaded from here.

opt_autosave_empty.message: No snapshots yet. One is taken when this browser's session syncs.

opt_autosave_search.message: Search snapshots by title or URL

opt_bm_export_desc.message: Netscape HTML opens in any browser's bookmark importer, Raindrop CSV imports into Raindrop, and the read-only page is one file a phone can open without the extension.

opt_bm_export_view_upload_confirm.message: The published page is a plain-text copy of your bookmarks and cannot be encrypted. Publish it anyway?

opt_bm_export_view_remove_confirm.message: Remove the published read-only page from your storage device? Your bookmarks are not affected.

opt_doctor_section_sub.message: Checks this browser's configuration and gives you a bundle that is safe to share.

opt_doctor_run_desc.message: Runs local checks only; no data leaves the device.

opt_doctor_copy_desc.message: The copied bundle holds versions, settings and the last error. Passphrases, tokens, passwords and full storage addresses are removed.

omnibox_default.message: Search Kesonode bookmarks, history and reading list

opt_cleanup_host_needed.message: Checking links needs permission to contact the sites in your bookmarks. Duplicates were still scanned.

opt_update_section_sub.message: Download the new zip, press the button once and Kesonode verifies, replaces and restarts itself. Firefox uses the upgrade script instead.

opt_update_check_desc.message: Checks GitHub only when you press the button. No settings, device info or sync data is sent.

opt_update_up_to_date.message: You are on the latest version, $VERSION$.

opt_update_failed.message: That did not work. Upgrading from a local package still works, or try again later.

opt_update_package_desc.message: Pick the zip you downloaded: its version and contents are verified, the install folder is updated and the extension restarts. On the first upgrade you choose that folder once.

opt_update_bad_zip.message: it is not a complete Kesonode package, or the file is damaged

opt_update_bad_unsafe.message: it contains unsafe paths and may have been tampered with

opt_update_bad_browser.message: it was built for a different browser

opt_update_bad_version.message: The package is not newer than the installed version, so there is nothing to upgrade.

opt_update_script_desc.message: Run it after downloading: it finds the zip, installs it into the folder named Kesonode and copies that path. If double-clicking does nothing, run it with sh from a terminal.

opt_update_steps.message:
Chromium: the first upgrade asks once for the folder Kesonode was loaded from. After that, press the button and pick the new zip.
Firefox: run the upgrade script. It always installs into the same Kesonode folder, so the extension ID and your settings are kept.

ai_privacy_notice.message: Off by default, with your own API key. A question sends only the bookmarks chosen on this device — a local text match on your question plus the most recently added ones, at most 120 entries, in small batches. Only titles, hostnames and folder paths leave the device; full URLs, history, tabs and your sync storage never do. The organisation plan looks only at bookmarks filed directly in a root, at most 400 of them. Kesonode has no server and never receives this data.

ai_enable_desc.message: While on, asking a question sends a reduced bookmark list to the provider configured below.

ai_base_url_desc.message: For example https://api.deepseek.com/v1. Requests go to /chat/completions on that host.

ai_api_key_desc.message: Stored on this device only. Never synced, never included in a settings export.

ai_status_ok.message: Connection works. Remember to save the settings at the bottom of the page.

ai_err_config.message: Fill in the API address, key and model name first.

ai_err_permission.message: Access to that address was not granted, so no request was sent.

ai_err_request.message: The model service did not answer. Check the address, key, model name and network.

ai_err_format.message: The model returned an unusable answer. Try again or use another model.

ai_err_snapshot.message: A restore point could not be created, so no bookmarks were changed. Configure a storage backend first.

ai_err_auth.message: The provider rejected the API key (401/403). Check the key and its quota.

ai_err_notfound.message: The endpoint or model name was not found (404). Check the base URL and model name.

ai_err_rate.message: The provider is rate-limiting requests (429). Wait a moment and try again.

ai_err_provider.message: The model service failed on its side (5xx). Try again later.

ai_organize_desc.message: The model suggests folders and possible duplicates. This only produces a list: you tick the rows, a pinned restore point is taken, and only then are bookmarks moved or removed.

ai_coverage_hint.message: The model saw $SENT$ of $TOTAL$ bookmarks this time; the rest were filtered out on this device.

ai_organize_duplicates.message: Possible duplicates (choose which one to keep)

ai_organize_applied.message: Applied. A restore point was taken first; these edits sync like any other bookmark change.

ai_popup_placeholder.message: Describe the bookmark you are looking for

ai_popup_no_report.message: There is no sync record to explain yet.

ai_save_notice.message: The switch and the fields below take effect after you save the settings at the bottom of this page.

ai_err_endpoint_scheme.message: That address cannot be used. It must be https, or http for this machine only (for example http://localhost:11434/v1).

ai_err_endpoint_credentials.message: Do not put a username or password in the address — use the API key field instead.

ai_popup_save_all.message: Save all to the reading list

ai_popup_saved_all_one.message: $COUNT$ page added to the reading list

ai_popup_saved_all_other.message: $COUNT$ pages added to the reading list

opt_update_dir_none.message: No folder bound yet. Choose the folder Kesonode was loaded from.

opt_update_dir_bound.message: Bound to “$NAME$”. Upgrades are written into this folder.

opt_update_dir_picking.message: Waiting for you to pick a folder…

opt_update_dir_unsupported.message: This browser (Firefox) does not let an extension write to a local folder. Download the upgrade script and run it instead.

opt_update_install_done.message: Version $VERSION$ is installed. The extension is restarting.

opt_update_err_no_permission.message: The browser no longer allows writing to that folder. Choose it again.

opt_update_err_not_installed.message: That folder has no manifest.json, so it is not a Kesonode install folder.

opt_update_err_key_mismatch.message: This package would change the extension ID, so your settings would be lost. Install it as a new extension instead.

opt_update_err_read.message: The installed manifest could not be read.

opt_update_err_write.message: Writing the new version failed. The folder still holds the old version; run the upgrade again.

opt_update_wait_folder.message: First upgrade: pick the folder Kesonode was loaded from in the browser dialog. This is needed once.

opt_update_wait_package.message: Choose the downloaded zip in the dialog. If you closed it, press the button again.

opt_update_check_unavailable.message: Release information is unavailable right now (the repository may be private). Upgrading from a local package still works.
